tagline: The city that rebuilt itself from rubble — a UNESCO-listed 'new' Old Town, neon museums, Vistula beaches and Europe's best pierogi prices.
overview: Warsaw was 85% destroyed in World War II — then rebuilt brick by brick from paintings and memory. The Old Town is so convincing it earned UNESCO status despite being younger than most of its visitors' grandparents.

The city balances that history with restless reinvention: the Palace of Culture (Stalin's gift) still towers over a skyline of new glass towers, the Neon Museum glows with communist-era signage, and the Vistula's wild left bank turns into beaches and bars each summer.
Speed's 2024 Europe tour streamed the Old Town to the usual fan crowds. Today's visitors find one of Europe's best-value capitals — serious museums, food and nightlife at prices that make Paris weep.

funFacts.title: REBUILT FROM PAINTINGS
funFacts.text: The Old Town was reconstructed using Canaletto's 18th-century cityscapes — a 'new' town that earned UNESCO status.

funFacts.title: STALIN'S GIFT
funFacts.text: The 237-metre Palace of Culture and Science is still Poland's most argued-about building.

funFacts.title: A RIVER LEFT WILD
funFacts.text: The Vistula's left bank is protected wilderness — beaches, bonfires and bar barges.

funFacts.title: THE UPRISING CITY
funFacts.text: The 1944 Warsaw Uprising lasted 63 days — every August 1 the city stops for a minute of silence.

funFacts.title: CHOPIN'S HEART
funFacts.text: His heart is sealed inside a Holy Cross Church pillar — smuggled home after his Paris death.
